# Signature

A handwritten signature that writes itself, stroke by stroke, at the pace a hand signs. Close a letter, a testimonial or a hero with it, or sign a Signature Pad and play the hand back.

```tsx
<span>Sincerely,</span>
<Signature viewBox="0 0 166 70" size="lg" aria-label="The Atelier team">
  <path d="M2 55.7C15 43.7 34.5 13.7 43 3.7C45.7 0.7 47.5 1.7 46.5 5.7C42.5 21.7 39.5 41.7 40.5 53.7C41.5 57.7 46.5 53.7 50 47.7C54.5 37.7 60 23.7 65 11.7C62 23.7 55.5 41.7 55 51.7C55 55.7 60 55.7 64.5 49.7C68.5 45.7 76 39.7 74.7 36.7C73.5 33.7 66.5 37.7 65.5 45.7C64.5 53.7 70 55.7 77.5 49.7C85.5 41.7 97 19.7 98 7.7C98.5 1.7 92 3.7 89.5 13.7C86 27.7 83 43.7 83 51.7C83 55.7 88 55.7 92.5 49.7C95.5 45.7 97.5 41.7 98.5 37.7C97 43.7 95.5 49.7 96.7 52.7C98 55.7 102.5 53.7 106.7 48.7C110.7 44.7 118 39.7 116.7 36.7C115.5 33.7 108.5 37.7 107.5 45.7C106.5 53.7 112 55.7 119.5 49.7C122.2 46.7 124.5 41.7 125.5 37.7C127 39.7 129 39.7 131.5 37.7C130 43.7 129.5 49.7 130.5 53.7C132 55.7 139.5 49.7 147.5 41.7" />
  <path d="M21.5 33.7C36.2 30.7 55.2 26.7 74 23.7" />
  <path d="M102 27.7C103.1 27.2 104.2 26.7 105.4 26.2" />
  <path d="M7 67.7C36.3 62.7 96.8 60.7 141.8 56.7C150 55.7 157.7 52.7 164 47.7" />
</Signature>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add signature
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/signature/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import { Signature } from "@/components/ui/signature"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Signature viewBox="0 0 166 70" aria-label="The Atelier team">
      <path d="M2 55.7C15 43.7 …" />
      <path d="M21.5 33.7C36.2 30.7 …" />
    </Signature>
  )
}
```

One `<path>` per pen stroke, in the order they were written: the word, the bar across the t, the dot on the i, the underline. The pen is the component's, so a path needs nothing but its `d`; ink, weight and round ends override whatever an SVG export wrote on it.

## Draw your own

Sign the pad, pick a speed and a size, and the Signature beside it writes your hand back. Every stroke you add plays the whole signature again, and the snippet under it is that exact drawing, ready to paste. Clear the pad to start from a blank page.

## Speeds

The whole signature takes the same time at a given `speed` however long the hand is, each stroke getting its share by length, so the pen keeps one pace and a short dot never crawls. `base` is a person signing without hurry; `fast` is for a small mark that should not hold up the page; `slow` is for a hero moment where the writing is the show. `delay` holds the pen for that many ms once the signature is on screen, so it can wait for whatever enters before it.

```tsx
<Signature speed="fast" viewBox="0 0 121 75" aria-label="Maya Chen">…</Signature>
<Signature viewBox="0 0 121 75" aria-label="Maya Chen">…</Signature>
<Signature speed="slow" viewBox="0 0 121 75" aria-label="Maya Chen">…</Signature>
```

## Sizes

`size` sets the height and the nib together: a small signature writes with a finer pen, so it keeps the weight of handwriting instead of turning into a marker line. The width follows the drawing. For any other height, pass an `h-*` class; the nib keeps its weight on screen however far the drawing is scaled.

```tsx
<Signature size="sm" viewBox="0 0 166 70" aria-label="The Atelier team">…</Signature>
<Signature viewBox="0 0 166 70" aria-label="The Atelier team">…</Signature>
<Signature size="lg" viewBox="0 0 166 70" aria-label="The Atelier team">…</Signature>
```

## In a testimonial

The signature is an image with a name, so it drops into any stack: between a [Testimonial](https://www.koalaui.com/docs/components/testimonials.md)'s quote and its byline, under a founder's letter, or as the last line of a Hero's sign-off. It hugs its drawing and follows its parent's alignment, so it sits left in a left-aligned card and centred in a centred one.

```tsx
<Testimonial variant="outline">
  <TestimonialQuote>We rebuilt the whole site in a week…</TestimonialQuote>
  <Signature size="sm" delay={200} viewBox="0 0 121 75" aria-label="Maya Chen">…</Signature>
  <TestimonialFooter>
    <TestimonialAuthor>
      <TestimonialName>Maya Chen</TestimonialName>
      <TestimonialTitle>Founder, Northwind</TestimonialTitle>
    </TestimonialAuthor>
  </TestimonialFooter>
</Testimonial>
```

## Already signed

`static` renders the finished signature with no writing: a signed document in a list, a receipt, anywhere the moment of signing has passed. It is also what everyone sees under `prefers-reduced-motion`, with or without the prop.

```tsx
<Signature static size="sm" viewBox="0 0 121 75" aria-label="Maya Chen">…</Signature>
<p>Signed by Maya Chen on 12 September 2026</p>
```

## API reference

### Signature

An `<svg role="img">` whose children are the strokes. Props: `aria-label` (required: what the signature says), `viewBox` (the drawing's box; leave it out and the signature fits itself to its ink on the client), `size` (`sm` · `md` · `lg`), `speed` (`fast` · `base` · `slow`), `delay` (ms, once on screen), `static`, plus every SVG prop. The ink is `currentColor`, so a `text-*` class recolours it; `className` is merged last.

### Timing

The three speeds live in `signatureDraw` in `lib/motion.ts`: the duration of the whole signature and the pause between two strokes, per speed. The writing starts when a tenth of the signature is on screen and runs once; give it a new `key` to write it again.

## FAQ

### How do I get the paths for my own signature?

Sign the pad in Draw your own above and copy the snippet, or use a Signature Pad in your own app. From Figma or Illustrator, export the signature as open strokes, one per pen stroke. An outlined (filled) signature has no centre line for the pen to follow.

### Why does it need an aria-label?

To a screen reader the drawing is an image, and an image of a signature with no name reads as nothing. The label is what the signature says ("Maya Chen", "The Atelier team"), and it is read out in its place.

### Why pass a viewBox if it can fit itself?

Fitting happens on the client, after the drawing is measured, so the width settles a moment after the page loads. With a viewBox the signature takes its exact width from the first paint and nothing around it moves.

### Does it wait until it is on screen?

Yes. A signature further down the page writes itself when a tenth of it scrolls into view, the same gate every entrance in Koala uses, and then only once.

### Can I change the ink colour?

The ink is currentColor, so any text colour class recolours it: text-muted-foreground for a quieter mark, or your own colour for a pen that is not black.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add signature` writes `components/ui/signature/`. Import from `@/components/ui/signature`:

- Components and helpers: `Signature`, `signatureVariants`
- Types: `SignatureProps`, `SignatureSpeed`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `in-view`, `motion`, `tv`
